summary: This standards-track RFC defines an X.509 certificate extension that holds information about how the certificate subject was authenticated by the issuing Certification Authority. It also defines one data structure to put in the extension.

eli5.summary: A certificate says who you are. This adds a note on how the issuer checked, like whether they saw your ID card or just an email.

questions: what is the authentication context certificate extension
how does x509 record saml authentication
what is a level of assurance in a certificate
can the authentication context extension be critical
subtitle: A certificate extension that records how the issuer authenticated the subject, with a SAML-based format.

tldr.problem: A certificate does not say how its subject was authenticated before it was issued, and the identity data in a certificate often differs in form from the identity data the issuer used.
tldr.mechanism: A new X.509 extension holds one or more authentication contexts, each with a URI naming its type and an optional data string. One defined type carries SAML details: the identity provider, the level of assurance and a mapping from SAML attributes to certificate fields.
tldr.outcome: A service can check how a signer was authenticated using only the certificate, while trusting only a list of CAs. Relying parties that do not understand the extension must assume the lowest allowed assurance level.

today: RFC 7773 is a Proposed Standard, published in March 2016. No obsoleting or updating RFCs are recorded for it.

sections.title: Why Record the Authentication Context
sections.content:
The goal is to let an application learn how a subject's identity in an X.509 certificate (RFC 5280) relates to the identity system that authenticated them. The identity may be held in the subject field, a subject alternative name or a subject directory attribute. In a typical case the user is authenticated through a SAML federation, and the user presents a SAML assertion in exchange for a certificate that can be linked back to it.

Such a certificate may have to follow a profile like RFC 3739, with attributes and value formats that differ from the SAML ones. The extension can record the identity provider, the level of assurance, the trust framework that defined it, a unique reference to the authentication instant, and a mapping between the SAML attributes and the certificate's subject information.

Without this, checking that a signer is the same user who logged in requires out-of-band knowledge about the CA and its practices, which does not scale. With the extension, a service provider only needs a list of trusted CAs.
sections.eli5: When your school ID is made from your online account, the ID looks different from the account. A note linking the two helps anyone who needs to be sure they are the same person.

sections.title: The Extension Syntax
sections.content:
The extension is a sequence of AuthenticationContext entries, each with a contextType and an optional contextInfo, both UTF8String. When the extension is present it MUST hold at least one entry.

The contextType MUST be a URI that identifies the context type and also the data format and encoding of the contextInfo. The extension MAY be marked critical. An application that meets a context type it does not understand MUST ignore it if the extension is non-critical and MUST reject the certificate if it is critical. If an application requires an authentication context and none is present or usable, the end-user certificate fails validation.

This RFC defines one type, for SAML; other documents can define others.
sections.eli5: The note has a label saying what kind of note it is. If you cannot read that kind of note, you may skip it, unless the issuer said the note is so important that you must refuse the ID.

sections.title: SAML Context Information
sections.content:
The SAML type is identified by the URI http://id.elegnamnden.se/auth-cont/1.0/saci. When it is the contextType, the contextInfo MUST be an XML document as a string of UTF-8 characters, following the schema in Appendix B. It SHOULD omit unnecessary line breaks and indentation to stay small, and it MUST NOT include an XML header.

The document has the root element SAMLAuthContext with child elements AuthContextInfo and IdAttributes.
sections.eli5: For the SAML kind of note, the details are written in a compact, standard format, with no extra spaces or fancy covers to waste room.

sections.title: The AuthContextInfo Element
sections.content:
This element MAY be present. It describes how the subject was authenticated. Its attributes are:

  • IdentityProvider (required): the SAML EntityID of the identity provider that authenticated the subject.
  • AuthenticationInstant (required): when the subject was authenticated.
  • AuthnContextClassRef (required): a URI from the assertion's AuthnStatement that identifies the context and the level of assurance.
  • AssertionRef (optional): a unique reference to the SAML assertion.
  • ServiceID (optional): an identifier of the service that verified the assertion.

It may also hold extra child elements for local conventions; these SHOULD be ignored if not understood.
sections.eli5: This part says who checked you, when, how carefully, and optionally which receipt and which service were involved.

sections.title: The IdAttributes Element and Attribute Mapping
sections.content:
This optional element holds one or more AttributeMapping elements. Each maps one certificate subject attribute or name form to a SAML attribute. It MUST have a Type: rdn (an attribute in a Relative Distinguished Name in the subject field), san (a name in the Subject Alternative Name extension) or sda (an attribute in the Subject Directory Attributes extension).

It also MUST have a Ref pointing to the field: an OID string for rdn and sda, and the explicit tag number for san (for example "1" for email address and "2" for dNSName), or an OID for an otherName. OIDs are written as integers separated by periods, such as 2.5.4.32, with no other characters.

Each mapping MUST contain a saml:Attribute element with a Name and optionally attribute values. With no value, the mapping only records which SAML attribute type supplied the certificate value. A value may differ in format from the certificate value: a SAML country of "Sweden" can appear in the certificate as "SE".

If several mappings point to the same certificate field, the RFC does not define which maps to which SAML attribute. Complex cases, such as several SAML attributes mapping to one certificate attribute, are not covered.
sections.eli5: It is a translation table. It says your name on the ID card came from the "full name" box in your online account, even if the two are written a bit differently.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The extension lets a CA outsource identifying and authenticating a subject to another trust infrastructure, dynamically and possibly differently for each certificate. Because the context is declared in the certificate, two certificates from the same issuer can have different levels of assurance.

A relying party therefore needs to know the certificate policy under which the CA operates in order to interpret the declared level. A relying party that cannot understand the extension MUST assume the certificate was issued at the lowest allowed level of assurance declared by the policy.
sections.eli5: Two IDs from the same office might have been checked with different care. If you cannot read the note, you have to assume the least careful check.
